body.statement: Can \(H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) produce one pure \(\epsilon\)-differentially private estimator, without knowing \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in\Theta_{\mathrm{sm}}\), whose risk is within the smallest possible logarithmic factor of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\) simultaneously across sparse and dense occupancy, and can a matching adaptive lower bound determine that factor?
body.justification: Unknown smoothness is the first deployment-level uncertainty after the fixed-class frontier is settled, and privacy may make its penalty regime dependent.
body.gap: Cai et al. characterize adaptation for federated density estimation, while Kennedy et al. leave nonprivate CATE adaptation open; no result combines nuisance elbows, occupancy, and pure central privacy.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether one private release can be tuned for individualized-effect analysis without disclosing or prespecifying smoothness.
